title: A biomimetic hydrogel culture system to facilitate cardiac reprogramming
protocol: Assemble slide glasses and silicone membranes as spacers as shown in the illustration (A).
Gently pour 1 mL polymerizing solution into the gap of the glass slide, being careful not to generate air bubbles.
Allow the solution to polymerize completely at room temperature.
Remove the slide glass after polymerization.
Peel off the gel from the glass slide.
Soak the hydrogel in a 10 mL MES buffer in a 100-mm cell culture dish.
Change the buffer solution three times.
Incubate the gel overnight (12–16 h) in a refrigerator at 4°C to hydrate completely.
Cut the polyacrylamide gel as needed for further use.
Activate the carboxyl group on the polyacrylamide gel surface.
Transfer the modified gel to culture plates coated with Matrigel.
Bond Matrigel covalently to the modified polyacrylamide gel.
Mix the reagents as shown in Table 2.
Cut the hydrogel to the same size as the well of a 12-well plate on a sheet of plastic wrap.
Immerse the cut-out round gel in MES buffer immediately after cutting.
Avoid contact and inhalation of NHS and EDAC.
Wear impermeable gloves and a lab coat when handling hazardous reagents.
Cut the hydrogel slightly smaller than the bottom of the cell culture plate.
Soak gel cutters in 70% ethanol after use and store.
Transfer the cut-out hydrogels to a 100-mm cell culture dish containing 10 mL of 0.5 M NHS/0.2 M EDAC solution.
Incubate samples for 30 min at room temperature to activate the carboxyl group in the polyacrylamide gel.
Shake the container to remove bubbles on the surface of the hydrogel.
Remove bubbles every 15 minutes during incubation.
Transfer the hydrogel to a 100-mm cell culture dish containing 10 mL of 60% methanol/PBS pre-cooled at 4°C.
Incubate for 2 h in a refrigerator at 4°C.
Transfer the hydrogel to a 100-mm cell culture dish on ice containing 10 mL of 0.05 mg/mL Matrigel/PBS solution.
Tap the gel to submerge it in the solution.
Continue tapping until the gel remains submerged in the solution.
Gently fix floating gels using a finger.
Transfer gels from the 100-mm culture dish to each well.
Add 500 μL of 0.05 mg/mL Matrigel/PBS to each well of the 12-well plate on ice.
Incubate for 16–18 h in the refrigerator set at 4°C for Matrigel conjugation.
Replace one-third of the Matrigel/PBS solution with PBS and incubate for 10 min in the refrigerator set at 4°C.
Repeat the replacement process three times.
Completely replace the Matrigel/PBS solution with PBS and incubate overnight (12–16 h) in the refrigerator set at 4°C.
Coat five 100-mm cell culture dishes with 0.1% gelatin/PBS.
Plate Plat-E cells at a density of 3.6 × 10^6 cells/dish in Plat-E transfection medium.
Incubate the plates at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Add 300 μL of OptiMEM to five 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Mix with 27 μL of Fugene6 in each tube and tap well with fingers.
Incubate the tubes at room temperature for 5 min.
Mix 9 μg of each retroviral DNA into the mixture by finger tapping.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 min.
Add the transfection mixture containing each retroviral DNA and Fugene6 to the culture medium.
Mix well by shaking the culture dish.
Incubate at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 24 h.
On day 2 for cardiac reprogramming, replace the medium containing the transfection mix with 10 mL of fresh Plat-E transfection medium.
Incubate at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 24 h.
On day 3 for cardiac reprogramming, collect each retroviral medium and filter through a 0.45-mm pore filter using a 10 mL sterile disposable syringe.
Mix 4 μL of polybrene with each retroviral medium to a final concentration of 4 μg/mL.
Prepare a cardiac reprogramming cocktail by mixing equal amounts of the retroviral medium of Gata4, Hand2, Mef2c, and Tbx5 (GHMT).

Culture of MEFs on Matrigel-based hydrogels and retrovirus infection requires careful handling to avoid aspirating the hydrogel when changing the medium. Use a 200 μL or 1,000 μL pipette to slowly change the medium.
On day 2 for cardiac reprogramming (the same day as step 27), remove PBS from the Matrigel-based hydrogel plate.
Tilt the plate to completely remove PBS between the plate and hydrogel.
Insert a tip into the gap between the well and the hydrogel and completely remove PBS with micropipetting.
Gently pour 1 mL of MEF medium into the hydrogel-attached wells.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min at room temperature.
Expose to UV light in a sterile hood for 30 min.
Remove the polystyrene lid during UV exposure.
Remove the MEF medium after UV exposure.
Seed MEFs at a density of 35,000 cells in 1 mL of MEF medium on Matrigel-based hydrogels for 12-well plate.
Filter the cultured MEFs through a 100-μm cell strainer to remove debris.
Incubate at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Replace the medium with 1 mL of reprogramming cocktail on day 3 for cardiac reprogramming.
Incubate at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
On day 4 for cardiac reprogramming, replace the reprogramming cocktail with 1 mL of iCM medium.
After 14 days of infection, replace the medium with FFV medium for iCM maturation.
Incubate at 37°C in 5% CO2 for one month to generate beating iCMs.
Assess the efficiency of cardiac reprogramming after 1 week using FACS.
Change the iCM medium every 2–3 days.
Replace FFV medium twice a week.
